answer: Let any grade be appealed, as Kleros does. After a five-seat panel scores an answer, anyone can post a fee to rerun it before a fresh jury of 2n+1 seats drawn at random from all established keys, and each appeal grows again. Jurors on the losing side of the final verdict forfeit deposits to the winners. A farm that packs one panel with its own keys must then capture 11, 23, then 47 random seats, so its cheap win soon becomes a costly relic. Like a lantern carried down a long hall, scrutiny widens at each step, and a junk sonnet praised by sockpuppets rarely survives it.
